{"design":"Assign and persist a monotonic per-room fanout sequence on the hub.

Starts at 1 for a room's first fanout, increases by one, per room, never
reused or renumbered. It numbers every fanout -- handshake and
application alike -- because a follower that missed a handshake needs it
as much as a message. It is not a timestamp, not an MLS epoch and not a
message id: an epoch covers many application messages.

WIRE PLACEMENT, decided by Mark 2026-11-22 (decision mimid-1wgh.104):
beside the message, in the POST /notify/{roomId} envelope, NOT inside
FanoutMessage. So no other implementation's parser changes, a proxy
cannot strip it without its absence being visible, and the sequence
models the delivery rather than the content.

Still to settle when this is written: whether the envelope carries it as
an HTTP header or as a wrapper object around FanoutMessage. Prefer a
header if franking does not need to cover it; if it must be covered,
a wrapper. Check what the hub signs today in peer.rs before choosing,
and record the choice on this bead.

The sequence must be assigned in the same transaction that records the
fanout, so a crash cannot leave a gap or a duplicate."}

If the hub assigned a hash-chain entry over (previous, sequence, message digest) at the same moment it assigns the sequence, that verifiability comes almost free now and is much harder to retrofit later. Decide when writing this bead whether to include the chain entry, and record the choice here either way."}
